title: feat(plugin-kanban,types): honour `columns[].collapsed` on the registered board (objectui#9628)
body:
Fixes #9628

Clause-②: no

## What this is

`KanbanColumn.collapsed` was declared on **both** published faces of the `object-kanban` arm — the lane element of `ObjectKanbanSchema` (`packages/types/src/objectql.ts` and its Zod mirror) and the runtime lane `KanbanColumn` (`complex.ts` and its mirror) — and read by `KanbanEnhanced` alone, a module no production source imports. An authored lane `{ "id": "todo", "title": "To Do", "collapsed": true }` parsed green on both faces and reached a board that did nothing with it.

This PR repairs it **at the reader** (dispatch direction 2). It does not retire the key and does not reopen the PASS verdict this card originates from.

## Direction-2 feasibility, measured before any repair

| question | reading |
|:--|:--|
| does the authored value reach the registered board? | **yes** — `bucketCardsIntoColumns` spreads `...col` on both legs, `localizeColumn` returns `{ ...col, title }`, and `KanbanRenderer` forwards the whole lane objects as `columns={processedColumns}` |
| does honouring move a published accept set? | **no** — both faces already declare the member; nothing that parsed before parses differently |
| does the protocol declare or refuse the key? | **neither** — `@objectstack/spec` `ObjectKanbanPropsSchema.columns` is `z.array(z.unknown()).optional()`, so the lane element is unconstrained at the protocol level (measured on the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 in this worktree) |
| would retiring it be cheap? | **no, and it is not this PR's route** — it narrows a published accept set (a maintainer floor) and would strand objectui#8801's tombstone, which names this key as where lane collapse lives |

## The reproduction, with its firing controls in the same run

`packages/plugin-kanban/src/__tests__/columnCollapsedHonoured-9628.test.tsx`, run against the **unrepaired** reader:

```
Tests  2 failed | 4 passed (6)
FAIL  renders the declared lane collapsed, with its cards withheld
      expected document not to contain element, found the card "Alpha"
FAIL  the viewer can expand it again
      Unable to find an accessible element with the role "button" and name "To Do"
```

The four that passed in that same run are the controls:

- both faces accept `collapsed: true` and keep the value (two legs), while an undeclared sibling key is accepted and **dropped** — so acceptance is a reading about this key, not about a passthrough;
- `className` authored on the **same** lane reaches the DOM, so the inert `collapsed` is not a plumbing failure of that lane;
- `limit` authored on a sibling lane paints the `Full` badge, so the board renders authored lane members at all.

## What an authored `collapsed: true` now does

The lane renders narrowed to a title spine with its cards withheld, on **both** of the board's layouts — the flat lane and the column cells of every swimlane row — and its heading becomes a disclosure the viewer can open. That is the meaning `KanbanEnhanced` already gave the key, so the platform states one behaviour for it rather than two.

The authored value is the lane's **initial** state. The board holds the viewer's overrides in a map and resolves them against the current prop, rather than copying the authored flags into state: `columns` is rebuilt on every data round-trip, so a state seeded from it would re-collapse a lane the viewer had opened on every refetch (AGENTS.md #8), and nothing here depends on the identity of a memoised value (#10).

**A board that authors the key nowhere is untouched.** The disclosure appears only on a lane that declared `collapsed: true`, so an omitted key and an authored `collapsed: false` stay indistinguishable. The one place this had to be defended by construction: `LaneHeading` returns the bare title where the caller already owns an element, because wrapping it in one more `span` unconditionally hands `laneCountHonesty-8307`'s count-badge locator the title instead. That was measured, not predicted — the first cut failed those four rows, and the fix is the `!collapsible` early return rather than a change to that pin.

## Prose this change falsified, and repaired

Three sentences asserted that on the board this arm renders, collapse is the viewer's and not the author's. That was true when objectui#8801 retired `allowCollapse`; this PR makes it false, so it is corrected where it is stated rather than left to publish:

- the `allowCollapse` tombstone docblock in `objectql.ts` and the author-facing refusal **message** on the Zod mirror — both keep every clause that ruling required of them (`KanbanColumn.collapsed`, "not a board-level authored toggle", "Delete the key"), and both now steer the author to a key that works. Swimlane-row collapse is still stated as the viewer's alone, because it still is;
- the **pending** changeset `.changeset/8801-object-kanban-allow-collapse-retired.md`, whose body publishes verbatim into the CHANGELOG at the next release — the same release this change lands in. Its "what replaces it: nothing you author" paragraph would have contradicted the entry beside it. `pnpm check:changeset-claims` is the instrument that put this in front of this seat.

The docblocks and `describe` text on the declaration itself, the plugin README and `content/docs/plugins/plugin-kanban.mdx` stop pointing authors at the unregistered board.

### Ablation of the pin this PR adds

From the committed tree, one leg each way, on `packages/plugin-kanban/src/KanbanImpl.tsx`:

```
PRE  anchor=1 inject=0 bytes=64403          anchor: "?? col.collapsed === true,"
POST anchor=0 inject=1 bytes=64400          inject: "?? false /* ABL9628 */,"
MUTATED_BLOB=3b3279af2eedf11b12eaea9b4dbfaf667f8d302a  HEAD_BLOB=6ecfdd141e9464476a89895d2102b7a19e0418eb
ABLATED_TEST_EXIT=1   Tests 3 failed | 4 passed (7)
```

The three that turned red are the flat lane, the viewer toggle and the swimlane layout; the four that stayed green are the two face legs, the undeclared-key control and the "no disclosure where nothing is authored" row — so the pin fails for the reason it exists and its controls do not move with it. Restored with `git checkout HEAD --` on that file's absolute path, proven by blob equality with `HEAD`, an empty `git diff HEAD`, a clean `git status` and the marker at zero occurrences. No ablation artefact remains in the tree.

An earlier attempt at the same leg is recorded rather than hidden: its `perl -0pi` replacement terminated at the `/` inside the injected comment, so the anchor went to zero while the intended marker never landed. The reading was voided and the leg re-run through a Python replacement that asserts the anchor count first — the numbers above are from that run.

## Acceptance notes

- **Serial constraints hold.** The surfaces this touches are `packages/types/src/complex.ts`, `objectql.ts`, their two Zod mirrors, `plugin-kanban/src/KanbanImpl.tsx`, the plugin README, one docs page and two `.changeset/` files. Intersection with objectui#7924 (`views.ts`), objectui#9375 (`base.ts`) and objectui#9712 (`data.ts`, `useViewData.ts`) is **empty**. Against the queued `.changeset/` PRs measured on their own file lists: objectui#9714 holds `8478-describe-line-addresses.md` and `8478-zod-pins-form-layout.md`, objectui#9715 holds `8499-node-slot-registered-arms.md` — none of the three is the file edited here.
- **`KanbanEnhanced` is untouched.** It keeps its own `collapsed` read and its two test importers (`cardPredicateScope.test.tsx`, `kanban-handler-slots-7664.test.tsx`). Whether it should be revived or deleted is objectui#8257's question, not this one's.
- Noted, not filed: `KanbanEnhanced`'s own collapse toggle is an icon-only `Button` with no accessible name, so on that board the control is unnamed to a screen reader. The repair here does not copy that shape — its disclosure is named by the lane title. No PR or person is queued on that file today, so the carrier is: none.
- Noted, not filed: `packages/types/src/complex.ts` introduces `KanbanColumn` as "a lane of the registered `'kanban'` renderer", a node key retired by objectui#8802. Stale framing in one sentence, not a defect in a declaration.
